findings.text: `syncHandlerEntries` reads `handlers.length` without a null check, and it now runs at the start of `forEach`, `use` and `eject`. `clear()` still guards with `if (this.handlers)`, so `handlers` can be null or undefined. If something sets `manager.handlers = null`, `forEach`, which `utils.forEach` used to handle silently, now throws a TypeError.

When `handlers.length` differs from the cached `handlersLength` (for example after external code splices `manager.handlers`), entries whose index no longer matches are deleted. A later `eject(id)` for a still-registered interceptor then silently does nothing, so the interceptor keeps running. The old index-based eject would have removed the entry at that position.

1.reason: After an external splice changes `handlers.length`, `syncHandlerEntries` deletes entries whose stored index no longer matches, so a later `eject(id)` for a still-registered interceptor finds no entry and does nothing.
